name.en: “Vote for my child” on WhatsApp: your account gets linked to a scammer

how.en: A message from someone you know asks you to vote for a child in a competition, or says they found a photo of you. The link goes to a page that looks genuine and asks for your phone number or shows a code with routine-looking instructions. Following them links the criminal’s device to your WhatsApp account (“GhostPairing”). The scammer can then read your chats and photos and message your contacts as you.

text.en: A friend or relative sends a link: vote for a child, or see a photo of you.
The page asks for your phone number or shows a code to enter.
Following the steps links the scammer’s device to your WhatsApp.
They read your chats and message your contacts as you.
Hi! My niece is in a photo competition, could you vote for her? It only takes a second, just confirm with your number: [link]

en: someone found a photo of you
whatsapp linked device i did not add
A link from a contact asking you to vote or view a photo.
A website asking for your phone number or showing a code for WhatsApp.
Don’t enter your number or codes on websites from links.
In WhatsApp, check Linked devices and remove any you don’t recognise.
Turn on two-step verification and warn your contacts.

sources.title: New WhatsApp scams trick users into giving scammers access to their accounts
